cron.description: 6-field Quartz cron of the tick. Cron runs in UTC, and a missed firing is dropped rather than caught up. It is an `override_params` entry on the node itself -- a FLAT params object, because a single-cell template has no inner cell to address -- or an `op` message at runtime.

schedule_id.description: The key the runtime ops (add/modify/remove/trigger) address this schedule by. It is a LITERAL UUID v7 and not a uuid7 substitution token: such a token is resolved at instantiation and has no filesystem-side producer, so a tree written straight to disk would refuse to boot on it, and a config that merely NAMES the token in its prose is refused the same way -- the substitution engine reads the whole file. A timer's key space is its own cell.db and this template ships exactly one schedule, so a minted id would buy nothing a constant does not. Two clocks in one colony may carry the same key and never meet.

description.purpose: A clock a manifest can name: one timer cell as a whole template, so a running colony can be given a periodic tick by a declaration instead of by a hand-built subtree. It sends, it decides nothing -- WHAT the tick means is the lane the parent's edge stamps on it.
description.use_when: Wherever something needs to happen on the minute rather than at the next touch: a firewall's in_sweep, a store's trim, any hive that measures time only when somebody knocks. Instantiate it under a name that says what it drives, and draw ONE edge out of it in the same mutation.
description.not_in_scope: No condition, no filter, no store, no catch-up. A clock that knew what it was ticking for would be a second scheduler, and a missed firing is dropped rather than replayed: the next tick asks the same question.
description.emits_meaning: A plain trigger. The body is empty because a clock has nothing to say; the six auto headers say which schedule fired and when, and the parent's edge names the lane.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove/trigger by schedule_id) as body.op -- the cadence is retunable at runtime without a restart.
examples: every five minutes -> the parent's edge stamps 'in_sweep' -> a firewall emits its expiry receipts on the minute instead of at the next touch
{"op": "modify", "schedule_id": "...", "cron": "0 0 * * * *"} -> the same clock ticks hourly from now on
no edge out of it -> the tick dead-letters as no_route naming the clock itself, because emit_to is '.' and an edge is what gives a tick a destination
